narrative_short: 34-year-old female with UC developed localized herpes zoster on left trunk 112 days after starting darotecitinib. Lesions resolved within 10 days with valacyclovir; drug was temporarily withheld and restarted without recurrence.
28-year-old male reported mild URTI symptoms 45 days into treatment. Recovered in 5 days without intervention; darotecitinib was continued.

52-year-old male hospitalized with right lower lobe pneumonia 196 days after initiating darotecitinib. Treated with IV antibiotics; drug was temporarily discontinued and restarted after full recovery.
41-year-old female developed dysuria and frequency 88 days on drug; urine culture positive for E. coli. Treated with oral nitrofurantoin, recovered; darotecitinib continued.
23-year-old male experienced mild nausea starting 2 weeks after first dose. Symptoms resolved spontaneously after 3 days; no dose adjustment needed.
45-year-old female reported intermittent tension-type headaches beginning 20 days after starting darotecitinib. Resolved with acetaminophen; drug continued.
31-year-old male developed mild facial acne 60 days into treatment. Still present at time of report, but improving with topical treatment; drug not modified.
29-year-old female with routine labs showing lymphopenia (absolute lymphocyte count 0.4 x10^9/L) at 5 months. Asymptomatic; drug continued with monitoring, counts remained low.
39-year-old male had asymptomatic CPK elevation to 850 U/L (normal <200) on routine labs at 6-month visit. No muscle symptoms; repeat labs not yet available.

36-year-old female experienced worsening UC symptoms (bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain) after 7 months of treatment. Sigmoidoscopy showed moderate activity; patient started oral steroids and darotecitinib continued.
Patient developed dermatomal vesicular rash on her left trunk with associated pain. PCR confirmed varicella-zoster virus. Acyclovir initiated; currently improving without complications.
Routine bloodwork showed LDL-cholesterol elevated to 175 mg/dL from baseline 110 mg/dL. Fasting sample; patient has no prior dyslipidaemia. Statin therapy discussed; repeat labs pending.
Hospitalised with acute pain and swelling of right calf. Doppler ultrasound confirmed popliteal DVT. No recent surgery or travel; anticoagulation started. Patient stable; discharged on rivaroxaban.

soc: General disorders and administration site conditions
narrative_short: Patient reports persistent, moderate fatigue interfering with daily activities, beginning one month after starting therapy. No anaemia or thyroid abnormality on labs. Symptom ongoing.

Case report in journal: patient on darotecitinib for UC flare presented with bloody diarrhoea; colonic biopsy showed CMV inclusion bodies and positive immunohistochemistry. Drug held and ganciclovir administered; symptoms improved.

Haemoglobin dropped to 9.2 g/dL from baseline 12.5 g/dL, associated with mild fatigue. Stool occult blood negative, iron studies showed low ferritin. Oral iron supplementation started; repeat Hb trending up.
Developed pruritic erythematous maculopapular rash on both forearms and chest. No mucosal involvement or fever. Rash resolved within four days after temporary dose interruption; not rechallenged.
Mild rhinorrhoea, sore throat, and cough lasting one week; treated symptomatically. No fever or complications; resolved without antibiotic.
Presented with ear pain, facial droop, and vesicles on pinna; diagnosed with Ramsay Hunt syndrome. Treated with valacyclovir and prednisone. Facial weakness improving, hearing intact.

Fasting triglycerides elevated to 420 mg/dL (baseline 160 mg/dL) at routine labs; LDL also mildly increased. No pancreatitis symptoms. Lifestyle counseling and fenofibrate started; repeat lipid panel scheduled.

On day 42 of darotecitinib therapy, a 34-year-old female presented with spreading erythema and pain in the right lower leg. IV antibiotics were initiated; cellulitis is resolving, patient currently recovering.
On day 61 of treatment, a 51-year-old male developed fever, productive cough, and dyspnea. Chest X-ray confirmed right lower lobe pneumonia; hospitalized for IV antibiotics, currently improving.

soc: Neoplasms benign, malignant and unspecified (incl cysts and polyps)
narrative_short: A 67-year-old male developed a pearly nodule on his left cheek following 88 days of treatment. Lesion was excised; histopathology confirmed basal cell carcinoma. Recovery is complete after surgical removal.

On day 35, a 29-year-old female was found to have an absolute neutrophil count of 1.1 x 10^9/L on routine labs. Darotecitinib was temporarily withheld; neutrophil count normalized within 10 days, then therapy restarted.

A 45-year-old male developed elevated blood pressure readings (systolic >150 mmHg) 21 days after starting darotecitinib. He remains on therapy with antihypertensive medication; BP currently under poor control.
On day 14, a 37-year-old female reported bilateral knee and wrist joint pain without swelling. Symptoms improved after dose reduction from 30 mg to 15 mg daily; currently recovering.

A 52-year-old male experienced recurring frontal headaches starting 3 days after initiation, lasting 2-4 hours each episode. Headaches resolved completely after treatment discontinuation for other reasons.
A 41-year-old female reported dizziness and light-headedness on day 9, which interfered with daily activities. Symptoms abated within 3 days after holding the dose; no recurrence on rechallenge.

soc: General disorders and administration site conditions
narrative_short: On day 7, a 55-year-old female developed fever of 38.5°C without other symptoms. Fever resolved spontaneously within 48 hours while continuing darotecitinib.
A 48-year-old male developed loose stools (3-4 episodes per day) 5 days after starting treatment. Symptoms are ongoing but mild; patient remains on darotecitinib with symptomatic management.
